correctness.rationale: PASS. The Heawood graph is bipartite between seven Fano points and seven Fano lines, so each class faces exactly the Fano line-cover condition on the opposite class; the two sides are independent. A 2-subset-of-four labeling of 7 points repeats a label on a unique point pair after the local proof: if p,q repeat A, their third collinear point r must carry A-complement. The four remaining Fano points form a 4-cycle under four lines through p,q, with two r-lines pairing diagonals. Incidence requirements force each of the four color names to occur at least twice among four off-line pair labels; the total exactly eight incidences forces all lower bounds to equality, complementary name pairs occupy distinct cycle diagonals, and there are exactly 2·2·2=8 completions per repeated-point-pair and repeated-color-label. All six labels then appear exactly once except repeated A. Hence 21·6·8=1008 independent possibilities per side. Four named sets are always distinct, so the S4 action is free and quotienting by 24 yields 42,336. The pair-stabilizer subgroup in GL3(F2) has order 8; its action on four distinct off-line labels is free and hence transitive. Independent exhaustive enumeration checked all 6^7=279936 seven-point colorings and found 1008 valid, evenly 8 per each of 126 duplicate-pair-label choices. This is a complete finite proof as well as a finite cross-check.

The exact witness count, unique repetition pattern, and complete orbit classification quantify a distinguished existence theorem at its sharp incidence configuration. The structural eight-completion lemma is reusable for other Fano label enumeration questions. It is not a routine division by 24: deriving the 1008 one-side count and proving freeness are substantive.
